Use SI units: $\hbar>0$ is the adopted reduced Planck constant, with action dimension $M L^2 T^{-1}$ and unit joule second ($\mathrm{J}\,\mathrm{s}$); the matrices $J_i$ and the angles are dimensionless. Thus $S_i$, $S_n$ and their outcome values have angular-momentum dimension $M L^2 T^{-1}$ and are read in $\mathrm{J}\,\mathrm{s}$. No numerical value of $\hbar$ is used. By the spin assignment of P6 with $s=\tfrac12$, the spin operators are $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ with $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ for the Pauli matrices in this basis ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii), [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)).

For a unit vector $n=(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta)$, $0\le\theta\le\pi$, put
$$u(\theta):=\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\,e_{+}+\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\,e_{-},\qquad v(\theta):=-\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\,e_{+}+\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\,e_{-}.$$
Then $u(\theta)$ and $v(\theta)$ are orthonormal and
$$S_{n}:=n\cdot \mathbf S=\frac{\hbar}{2}(\sin\theta\,\sigma_{x}+\cos\theta\,\sigma_{z}),\qquad S_{n}u(\theta)=\frac{\hbar}{2}u(\theta),\qquad S_{n}v(\theta)=-\frac{\hbar}{2}v(\theta).$$

[F3] **Outcome law and update.** For a declared ideal sharp measurement with projections $P_{a}$ the probability of the outcome $a$ in a state $\rho$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ for a pure preparation $[\psi]$, and the conditional state after a positive-probability outcome is $\rho_{a}=P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clauses (a)-(b), [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] clauses (a)-(b)).

These are stipulated for the finite polarization space, beyond the massive-matter sector of P1; they are not consequences of its massive-particle assignment. Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the mathematical suppliers. Fix a propagation label $k_0\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ relative to fixed Euclidean spatial coordinates, and a real orthonormal transverse pair $v_x,v_y\in\mathbb R^3$ with $k_0\cdot v_x=k_0\cdot v_y=0$. Its state space is $D(H)$ and a unit ray $[\psi]$ represents $T_{\psi,\psi}$ for $\|\psi\|=1$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]). The identification of these unit rays as polarization preparations is the adopted finite assignment, motivated by the source account in Binney and Skinner, Section 1.3.6, printed pages 14-15. It supplies no photon number or radiation dynamics. Angles are dimensionless, read in radians. For a real angle $\alpha$ put
$$e_{\alpha}:=\cos\alpha\,e_{x}+\sin\alpha\,e_{y},\qquad e_{\alpha}^{\perp}:=-\sin\alpha\,e_{x}+\cos\alpha\,e_{y}.$$
The **ideal analyser** $A(\alpha)$ is the declared ideal sharp measurement with the two outcomes transmit and block, whose projections are $T_{e_{\alpha},e_{\alpha}}$ and $T_{e_{\alpha}^{\perp},e_{\alpha}^{\perp}}$ respectively, with outcome and update rules stipulated in [F2] below ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

[F1] **The analyser is a declared ideal sharp measurement.** $T_{e_{\alpha},e_{\alpha}}$ and $T_{e_{\alpha}^{\perp},e_{\alpha}^{\perp}}$ are orthogonal projections with sum $I$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clause (c), [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (a)).

[F2] **Adopted outcome law and update.** On the finite polarization space independently assigned above, stipulate the projective probability and conditional-update rules in the form of P3: for mutually orthogonal projections $(P_a)$ summing to $I$, outcome $a$ has probability $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$ and its conditional state is $P_a\rho P_a/p_a$ only when $p_a>0$. These are adopted apparatus assumptions, using the formulas and vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clauses (a)-(b), rather than a deduction extending the massive-matter scope of P1. For a pure preparation $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$, the probability is $\|P_a\psi\|^2$ by [F3]; for $p_a>0$ the conditional state is the pure state of $P_a\psi$ normalized, by [[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]] clause (d).

- **Idealisation.** Each analyser is represented by the declared ideal sharp measurement of clause (c) of [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]: the blocked component is not available for later experiments and the transmitted component leaves the analyser in the corresponding pure state. A physical Polaroid or polarizing beam splitter has its own absorption, reflection, efficiency and background behaviour, which this example does not model.
- **No radiation model.** The two-level space rather than a quantized radiation mode is the declared model; no photon number, mode function, field quantization or Maxwell dynamics is asserted, and no position or arrival-time information is described.
- **Sampling.** The numbers $1,\tfrac12,\tfrac14$ are single-trial model probabilities. To describe a run of $N\ge1$ trials one must additionally specify a joint sampling law. For example, independent Bernoulli variables $X_1,\ldots,X_N\in\{0,1\}$ with $\mathbb P(X_j=1)=q$ encode identical transmit trials at a stated probability $q$; their frequency is $f_N=N^{-1}\sum_jX_j$. Even for this sampling model a particular finite frequency need not be close to $q$: at $q=1/4$ the all-blocked and all-transmitted runs have probabilities $(3/4)^N>0$ and $(1/4)^N>0$. Identical single-trial probabilities alone specify no joint sampling law. No trial data or inference is reported here.

By [L1] this maximal mathematical geodesic is the straight line $x(\gamma(s))=x_0+sv$. With proper-time parametrization $\tau=s/c$ (the normalization $\lambda=1$ of [L1]), this is $x(\gamma(\tau))=x_0+c\tau v$; the coordinate velocity is the constant $w=(c/v^0)(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ with $|w|<c$ by [L1]. This proves (b). [A3, L1, given, algebra]

Instead, fix a metric state set $(X,d)$, for example a subset of phase space with the Euclidean distance, on which every Verlet stage is defined and $V_h:X\to X$. Require a positive step $h>0$, a separately established map bound $d(V_h(x),V_h(y))\le(1+L_{\mathrm{map}}h)d(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in X$, $L_{\mathrm{map}}\ge0$, and computed points $x_j\in X$ with $x_0=z_0$ and $d(x_{j+1},V_h(x_j))\le\eta$. The exact scheme iterates are $z_{j+1}=V_h(z_j)$. [[lem-cm-roundoff-accumulation-in-one-step-schemes]] then gives
$$d(x_n,z_n)\le\eta\frac{(1+L_{\mathrm{map}}h)^n-1}{L_{\mathrm{map}}h}\le\eta e^{L_{\mathrm{map}}T}\frac{T}{h}\qquad(nh\le T,\ L_{\mathrm{map}}>0),$$
with $d(x_n,z_n)\le n\eta\le\eta T/h$ if $L_{\mathrm{map}}=0$. For a readout $F:X\to\mathbb R$ with $0\le\Lambda<\infty$ and $|F(x)-F(y)|\le\Lambda d(x,y)$, multiply these bounds by $\Lambda$. The constant $L_{\mathrm{map}}$ is a bound for the numerical map, not the exact-field derivative constant $L$ of the preceding section; that flow bound does not establish the map hypothesis.
To combine discretization and implementation bounds, take $X$ to be a
subset of the declared numerical phase domain and additionally require
$y_j\in X$ for $0\le j\le n$. Require either that $d$ is the Euclidean
distance used for discretization, or a finite constant $c_d\ge0$ with
$d(u,v)\le c_d\lVert u-v\rVert$ for all $u,v\in X$; in the Euclidean case
set $c_d=1$. Let $D_n$ and $I_n$ denote the displayed discretization and
implementation upper bounds, respectively, with all their hypotheses and a
common positive step satisfied. Then the triangle inequality in $(X,d)$
gives $d(x_n,y_n)\le d(x_n,z_n)+d(z_n,y_n)\le I_n+c_dD_n$.
For the readout $F$ above, evaluated in these same numerical state
coordinates, $|F(x_n)-F(y_n)|\le\Lambda(I_n+c_dD_n)$. A multi-time
readout requires a Lipschitz bound in a declared product-state metric and
comparison bounds in that metric for the ordered state tuples. A common
underlying set alone supplies no comparison between metrics.
The number $\eta$ is a
**hypothesis on the per-step residual**, not a measurement of an arithmetic
unit, and the lemma says nothing about the distribution of rounding.

**The two computations.** [[ex-nrqm-interference-ideal-flat-two-path-screen-distribution]]
computes, in the declared two-path model with flat product-form amplitudes, the
exact coherent and which-path probabilities of the overlap and outer regions of
the declared detection coordinate: at relative phase $\pi$ the coherent law
assigns probability zero to the whole overlap region while the balanced
which-path law assigns it positive probability, and a slab bin
$B_1\times\mathbb R^2$ has positive coherent probability at that phase
exactly when $|B_1\cap(I_1\triangle I_2)|>0$, where $I_1,I_2$ are the
declared intervals and $I_1\triangle I_2$ is their symmetric difference
(the two outer regions). Mere nonempty intersection does not suffice.
[[ex-nrqm-interference-uniform-phase-averaging]]
shows that for orthogonal path components a declared ensemble whose relative
phase is uniformly distributed over the finitely many $n$-th roots of unity has
the which-path law with the norm weights as its averaged law. Both are
conditional computations in the declared model under all the stated supplier
hypotheses, including Countable Choice and Choice, and the pair's detection laws
([[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]]); neither is a
dynamics, an environmental decoherence model, a detector response or a
statement about an apparatus.
consumer_reviews.reason: The screen audit already requires positive overlap measure rather than mere nonempty intersection, and phase averaging uses orthogonal components with norm weights. Those clauses match the changed suppliers and retain their choice assumptions.

**What is established.** The page declares the two-path preparation model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] with its
path components, coherent and which-path preparations and ideal detection bins,
and the recorded detector and sampling model
[[def-nrqm-interference-recorded-detector-and-sampling-model]] with its bounded
effects, no-record channel, loss conditioning and declared independent trials.
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]] derives the
normalized coherent bin law with its amplitude cross term, the which-path bin
law, and the criterion under which the two declared laws coincide on every bin;
the criterion comparing phase $0$ is conditional on the model being admissible
at phase $0$.
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-recorded-bin-laws-loss-and-conditioning]] derives the
recorded-bin laws, the no-record mass and conditioned law, the reduction of
indicator weights to ideal bins, and a sufficient condition for the recorded
laws to coincide when the model is admissible at phase $0$.
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-continuity-and-local-probability-balance]]
derives the continuity equation and local squared-amplitude balance for
componentwise $C^1$-in-time, $C^2$-in-space solutions of the P4/P5 equation
almost everywhere with the bounded measurable P5 potential. This density is a
position probability density when the full-space state is normalized; under
the theorem's domination and surface-flux hypotheses its finite total
squared-amplitude integral is conserved on an interval. P4 separately gives
norm conservation of the model's flow and total probability one for unit
preparations.
[[texp-nrqm-interference-finite-sample-fringe-failure]] shows that, within the
declared independent-trials model, a declared fringe criterion that rejects a
positive-probability outcome sequence fails with positive probability, and
that no criterion distinguishes two recorded laws that coincide.
consumer_reviews.reason: The interference audit explicitly retains phase-zero admissibility, loss conditioning and independent sampling assumptions. Its continuity and conservation summary is domain-qualified and does not infer dynamics or detector validity from a fringe law.

[[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] is the page's
mathematics: the explicit factorisation of the single-vertex emission
kernel, the normalised photon-energy law, its concentration at the transition
energy for a continuous positive mode density, and the strict positivity of
the law on windows of positive density.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-emission-and-absorption-coefficients]]
proves the single-vertex emission and absorption amplitudes of the model, the
exact-model control of the one-photon level-$b$ projection probability by the
explicit Dyson tail, and the exact mirror relation between emission into and
absorption from a unit one-photon vector.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]] proves the
limit of the single-vertex coefficient per unit time and declares the model
rate coefficient $\Gamma_{b}=2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}J_{b}(\Delta)/\hbar$ under a
continuous positive mode density, with the above-cutoff case tending to zero.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-stimulated-dipole-drive-transitions]] proves the
first-order amplitudes of the prescribed classical drive, the equal
stimulated emission and absorption coefficients for the same physical gap and prescribed real field, and
the exact identification of declared two-level Pauli data with the circular
and linear two-level drive models of the driven-dynamics page.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-dipole-selection-rules]] proves the necessary
angular and parity conditions on the uncompressed dipole matrix elements, and
transfers their vanishing to compressed matrices when the declared finite-level
subspace is spanned by a finite subfamily of bound states and its declared
orthonormal basis is chosen from that same subfamily. All of these are
conditional consequences of the cited postulates, mathematics and model data;
their units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

affected_use: **What is proved.** [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] identifies the atoms of the spectral measure with the eigenspace projections, so that an exact value has zero probability unless it is an eigenvalue. [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] identifies the support of the spectral measure with the spectrum, giving the precise reading of the statement that an outcome lies in the spectrum. [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] proves affinity under statistical mixtures and uniform trace-norm continuity. [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]] assembles the mean, second moment and variance formulas with their exact domain criteria, and [[lem-nrqm-observables-states-separated-by-bounded-projections]] proves that distinct states are separated by the law of a rank-one projection. The physics theorems read these results as conditional statements about assigned observables: [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] (the law is a probability measure, affine in mixtures, atomic only at eigenvalues, supported in the spectrum and not assumed to have a density), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] (moments exist exactly under the stated domain hypotheses), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-position-and-momentum-outcome-laws]] (the joint position density $|\psi|^{2}$ and the momentum-coordinate density obtained from the frequency density $|\mathcal F_2\psi|^{2}$ by taking its marginal and the Jacobian factor $(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}$) and [[pthm-nrqm-observables-states-separated-by-born-statistics]] (distinct preparations differ in some bounded observable's statistics; all such exact laws uniquely determine the preparation within the model).

[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-free-translation-and-momentum]] is the exact free-model
computation: with $V\equiv0$ every translation is a symmetry, the free flow in
the momentum representation is the unimodular multiplier
$M_{f_{t}}$, $f_{t}(p)=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$, the translations are the
multipliers $M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$, and the momentum components are
conserved sharp observables with the law, moment and generator statements of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]];
the modulus of the momentum representative is invariant in time almost
everywhere.
[[cex-nrqm-symmetries-nonconstant-potential-breaks-translation]] shows that
translations need not remain symmetries for nonconstant potentials:
for the bounded measurable potential energy $E_{*}1_{B(0,R)}$, with
$E_{*}>0$ in J and $R=1\,\mathrm m$, no nonzero translation is a symmetry,
because the shifted potential differs from the original on a set of positive
measure, so the symmetry criterion of the translation theorem is not met.
For a specified translation $a$, the criterion is exactly
$V(\cdot-a)=V$ almost everywhere; nonconstancy in a direction alone does
not exclude discrete translations along that direction.
[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-parity-selection-rule]] derives, for a potential even
almost everywhere, that every energy eigenspace is invariant under the parity
action, that a nondegenerate eigenstate has definite parity, and that the
position matrix element of two states of equal parity vanishes.

almost-everywhere rotational and parity invariance of a bounded radial
potential and instantiates
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]]: all rotations are
symmetries, the rotation action is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry
group, and the coordinate-rotation generators $L_{i}$ are conserved sharp
observables, with the underlying conservation mechanism of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]].

In Minkowski spacetime $(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ with metric
$\eta=-dt^2+dx^2$ and time orientation $\partial_t$, let $q:=(1,0,0,0)$ and
$0<\tau_0<1$. The time separation from $q$
([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) is
$$\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{(t-1)^2-|x|^2}\qquad\text{for }r=(t,x)\in J^-(q),$$
and equals $0$ otherwise. Then the level set
$$S:=\{r\in I^-(q):\tau_q(r)=\tau_0\}$$
is a smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface, every causal curve meets it in
at most one parameter value, and every point of $S$ is the past endpoint of
a future-directed timelike geodesic segment of length $\tau_0$ ending at $q$, namely the radial
segment $s\mapsto r+\frac{s}{\tau_0}(q-r)$ for $s\in[0,\tau_0]$, where
$r=(1-\sqrt{\tau_0^2+|x_s|^2},x_s)$.

[L1] Time separation: $\tau_q$ is finite on $J^-(q)$, for $r\ne q$ the supremum over causal curves is attained on the causal geodesic image; at $r=q$ the value is zero with the explicitly declared constant degenerate-geodesic convention, and in a causally convex normal neighbourhood of $q$ one has $\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{-g_q(\exp_q^{-1}r,\exp_q^{-1}r)}$ ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]] clauses (a)-(c)).

## Verification
1.1 (The distance formula.) For $r\in J^-(q)$ the displacement $q-r=(\Delta t,\Delta x)$ is causal, and for $r\ne q$ the unique maximizing geodesic image is the straight causal segment, whose length is $\sqrt{(\Delta t)^2-|\Delta x|^2}=\sqrt{(t-1)^2-|x|^2}$ when the displacement is timelike; for nonzero lightlike displacement the value is $0$; for $r=q$ the degenerate constant-geodesic convention also gives zero; this is the Minkowski instance of the attainability and geodesy of maximizers in [[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]] clause (a). [given, L1, algebra]

3.1 (At most one meeting along a causal curve.) Since $\tau_q$ is continuous and $g(\nabla\tau_q,\cdot)$ has no nonzero causal kernel on $U$, the function $t\mapsto\tau_q(\gamma(t))$ is strictly monotone along every causal curve segment contained in $U$; hence such a segment meets the level $\tau_0$ in at most one parameter value, and a causal curve segment with $\tau_q$-values straddling $\tau_0$ meets $S$ at least once by the intermediate value theorem ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]] clause (b), [[def-continuity-real]]). If a causal curve met $S$ in two parameter values, the subsegment between them would join two points of $S$ with equal $\tau_q$-value, contradicting strict monotonicity; if the subsegment left $U$ it would contain a point $p$ with $\tau_q(p)=0$, that is $p\not\ll q$; but $p\le\gamma(t_2)\ll q$ and push-up gives $p\ll q$, a contradiction ([[lem-gr-push-up-rule]], [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). - **What is proved.** [[pthm-gr-linearized-field-equations]] derives the
  linearized field equation and its vacuum branch by differentiating the
  adopted field law [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] along a smooth family of
  exact solutions. Its separate quadratic residual bound follows from the
  mathematical Taylor estimate for the Einstein tensor once
  $G^{(1)}(h)=0$; it does not require $\eta+\lambda h$ to belong to an exact
  solution family. The all-space harmonic-gauge existence clause additionally
  assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The mathematical
  existence statement for the vacuum plane waves is
  [[thm-gr-tt-plane-wave-solutions]]: for every pair of bounded smooth
  profiles there is an exact solution of the linearized vacuum equations in
  harmonic gauge, whose exact metric in the zero-source, $\Lambda=0$ branch
  has vacuum field-law residual bounded by a constant times the square of the
  amplitude on nonempty compact sets. [[pthm-gr-plane-wave-polarizations]] reads the amplitude
  classification of [[lem-gr-plane-wave-gauge-decomposition]] as the
  statement that the model has two polarization types at fixed null wave covector,
  with the gauge-invariant first-order curvature coefficients as their
  geometric content; no operational observable is defined on this page.
  [[pthm-gr-plane-wave-tidal-detector-response]] derives the model's
  infinitesimal relative-acceleration law for a geodesic variation and the
  finite path-length strain of the ideal two-body detector of
  [[def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling]].

- **Frame and gauge caveats.** The transverse-traceless form and the
  amplitudes $A_+,A_\times$ are defined with respect to an adapted
  orthonormal frame ([[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]],
  [[lem-gr-plane-wave-gauge-decomposition]]); the pair $(A_+,A_\times)$
  transforms under screen rotations as in
  [[lem-gr-tt-screen-projector]] clause (d), and the space of classes, not
  the particular representative, is the frame-independent content. The
  first-order curvature is gauge invariant
  ([[thm-gr-tt-plane-wave-curvature]] clause (b)). The projection to the
  physical screen is two-dimensional; a trace subtraction with the half
  weight of a three- or four-dimensional projector is not the
  transverse-traceless projection
  ([[lem-gr-tt-screen-projector]] remark and the counterexample recorded
  there).

On that vocabulary the page's first physics theorem,
[[pthm-cm15-central-scattering]], transfers the finite-range scattering theory
of [[cm-math-central]] to the model: under a finite-range $C^2$ potential and a
simple outer turning point, the relative coordinate of a model motion extends
uniquely to all of time, with a single apsis and two monotone branches; the
asymptotic velocities exist with speed $\sqrt{2E/\mu}$; beyond the range the
motion is exactly free and the incoming and outgoing lines have perpendicular
distance $b=J/\sqrt{2\mu E}$; the half-angle advance is the quadrature
$\Delta=\int_{r_*}^{\infty}J\,\mathrm dr/(r^2\sqrt{2\mu(E-V)})$ and the
asymptotic directions satisfy the deflection relation with angle
$\pi-2\Delta$ when $0<\Delta<\pi/2$; and on a smooth deflection branch that
records the model's deflections the outgoing angular measure carries the
cross-section density, with the uniform-incident rate reading attached. Its
scope clause records that no monotonicity, injectivity or completeness of the
deflection map is asserted.
[[pthm-cm15-rutherford-model]] separately treats the long-range the repulsive $\kappa/r$
potential: the effective potential is strictly decreasing, every stated
relative motion extends without collision to all of time, the deflection map
is the single $C^1$ branch $2\arctan(\kappa/(2Eb))$ with inverse
$(\kappa/2E)\cot(\theta/2)$, the differential cross-section is the Rutherford
density $(\kappa/4E)^2\csc^4(\theta/2)$, every angular band has the finite
truncated total $\pi(b(\theta_1)^2-b(\theta_2)^2)$, and the ideal total
diverges at forward angles. The parameter $\kappa$ is a model datum of the
mechanical model and is not identified with any electromagnetic quantity.

**Gauge classification and polarizations.**
[[lem-gr-plane-wave-gauge-decomposition]] fixes an adapted orthonormal frame
from a null wave covector and proves the exact decomposition
$V_0=T\oplus G$ of the harmonic-gauge amplitude space into the pure
plane-wave gauge amplitudes and the transverse-traceless amplitudes, with a
unique TT representative of every class for each real phase coefficient.
The quotient for one cosine or sine coefficient is two-dimensional, with the
amplitudes $(A_+,A_\times)$ of the TT representative as linear coordinates;
the full real cosine-and-sine pair has two such copies, four real
coefficients for the two polarization types. [[ex-gr-plane-wave-regauge-to-tt]] works the explicit regauging
of a non-TT amplitude. [[thm-gr-tt-plane-wave-solutions]] shows that TT
planar perturbations with arbitrary bounded smooth profiles solve the
linearized vacuum equations, are in harmonic gauge, and give small-amplitude
Lorentzian metrics whose exact zero-source, $\Lambda=0$ vacuum residual is
bounded by a constant times the square of the amplitude on nonempty compact
sets.
[[thm-gr-tt-plane-wave-curvature]] computes the first-order curvature
coefficient — in particular $R^{(1)}_{0i0j}=-\tfrac12\partial_0^2h_{ij}$ for
spatial planar waves — proves its gauge invariance, and identifies its
contraction with the linearized Ricci coefficient.
